chapter_title_en: Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
დაწერა თუ: “ჩემნო ყმანო, გამზრდელნო და ზოგნო ზრდილნო,
ერთგულნო და მისანდონო, ამას ზედა გამოცდილნო,
თქვენ ჩემისა საწადლისა მიდგომილნო, ვითა ჩრდილნო,
და წიგნი ჩემი მოისმინეთ, ყოვლნო, ერთგან შემოყრილნო!
stanzas.english_translation: "Hazard kills equally be it one or a hundred. Loneliness can matter naught if the group (? grouping) of the heavenly powers (? planets) protect me. If I come not hither in three years, then will it beseem thee to mourn and wear funeral garb. I will give thee a letter, whoever is my courtier must obey thee."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 165; Wardrop Stanza 163): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მიწაცა თქვენი ავთანდილ, ისმინეთ, გიწერ მა რასა,
თვით ვიქმ ხელითა ჩემითა ამა წიგნისა წერასა;
ცოტასა ხანსა ვარჩივე გაჭრა სმასა და მღერასა,
და პურად და საჭმლად მივენდე ჩემსა მშვილდსა და ცერასა.
stanzas.english_translation: He wrote as follows: "My vassals, my instructors and some my pupils, faithful, trusty and tried, attentive to my behests like shadows, hearken to my letter all assembled!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 166; Wardrop Stanza 164): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“საქმე რამე მიც თავისა ზე სადმე გარდსახვეწელი,
დავყო მარტოდ და ღარიბად ესე წლეული მე წელი,
გემუდარები ამისთვის, ვარ თქვენი შემომხვეწელი,
და მე დამახვედროთ სამეფო მტერთაგან დაულეწელი.
stanzas.english_translation: "Give ear! I, Avt’handil, earth beneath your feet, write this unto you; with mine own hand have I written this epistle. For a little while I have preferred roaming to drink and song; for bread and meat I shall trust to my bow and thumb.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 167; Wardrop Stanza 165): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე შერმადინ დამიგდია, ჩემად კერძად პატრონობდეს,
სიკვდილსა და სიცოცხლესა სადამდისცა ჩემსა სცნობდეს,
ყოვლთა მზეებრ მოგეფინოს, ვარდს არ ზრვიდეს, არ აჭნობდეს,
და შემცოდესა ყველაკასა, ვითა ცვილსა, დაადნობდეს.
stanzas.english_translation: "I have in hand a certain matter which makes me journey to a far country; I depart alone, and this year shall I travel. I ask you only this: I beseech you let me find the realm unshaken by the foe.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 168; Wardrop Stanza 166): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.english_translation: "I have appointed Shermadin to be lord in my stead; until he learn of my life or death he will shine upon you all like the sun; he will make the rose to be frosted and not fade, he will cause all misdoers to melt away like wax.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 169; Wardrop Stanza 167): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.english_translation: You know, too, how he has grown up with me like a brother and like a son; you must obey him as if he were Avt’handil; let him make to sound the trumpet, do everything as I have hitherto done; if I come not at the time appointed, mourning and not laughter will be seemly, to you."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 170; Wardrop Stanza 168): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ბრძანა: “წადით ყველაკაი, აქა მომხრედ არვინ მინა”.
მონებიცა მოიშორვა, თავი გაითავისწინა,
მარტო გარე შემობრუნდა, შამბი შიგან გაირბინა,
და მიწყივ მისად საგონებლად მისი მკვლელი თინათინ-ა.
stanzas.english_translation: The eloquent and nice-worded one ended this letter, he tied gold round his waist, habited himself to travel alone; he said: "I shall mount in the plain." The soldiers formed in line, then they came forth; he tarried no time indoors.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 171; Wardrop Stanza 169): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
იგი ველი გაირბინა, ლაშქართაგან გაეკიდა.
ვინმცა ნახა სულიერმან, ანუ ვინმცა გაეკიდა?
ვის მახვილი ვერას ავნებს, მისი მკლავი გაეკიდა,
და მისგან ტვირთი კაეშნისა ტვირთად ვარგად გაეკიდა.
stanzas.english_translation: He said: "Let all go hence; herein I need none as a partisan." He sent the slaves away also, he remained by himself, alone he withdrew himself, he hastened through the rushes. His slayer, T’hinat’hin, is always in his thoughts.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 172; Wardrop Stanza 170): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა ლაშქართა ინადირეს და პატრონი მოითვალეს,
იგი პირ-მზე ვეღარ ჰპოვეს, პირი მათი იფერმკრთალეს;
მათსა დიდსა სიხარულსა სამძიმარი ანაცვალეს,
და ყოვლგან რბოდეს საძებარად, ვინცა იყო უცხენმალეს.
stanzas.english_translation: He galloped over that plain; he was lost to the soldiers’ sight. Whatever human being might have seen him and pursued him, his sword could not harm him; his arm was hampered. He was heavy laden with a burden of grief for her sake.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 173; Wardrop Stanza 171): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ღმერთი, ლომო, შენად ნაცვლად სხვასა ვისცა დანერგვიდეს!”
დარბოდეს და სხვაგნით სხვათა მოამბეთა მოასხმიდეს;
ვეღარა ცნეს მისი საქმე, გაიარა აქათ კიდეს,
და მისნი სპანი გულ-მოკლულნი ცრემლსა ცხელსა გარდმოჰყრიდეს.
stanzas.english_translation: When the soldiers hunted and sought their lord, and could no longer find the sun-faced, their countenances paled, their great joy turned into heaviness, they ran everywhere to seek him, whoever had a swift horse,
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 174; Wardrop Stanza 172): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
შერმადინ ერთგან შეყარნა ხასნი და დიდებულები,
უჩვენა იგი უსტარი, ამბავი მისი თქმულები;
რა მოისმინეს, ყველაი დარჩა გულ-დანაწყლულები,
და თავსა იცემდეს, არ იყო გული უცრემლო, ულები.
stanzas.english_translation: O lion, whom can God put in thy place! They ran and brought out other messengers from elsewhere; they could learn nothing of him; he passed from that place. His disheartened hosts shed hot tears.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 175; Wardrop Stanza 173): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ყოვლთა ჰკადრეს: “თუცა ყოფა ჩვენ უმისოდ გვეარმისცა,
უშენოსა საჯდომი და ტახტი მისი ვისმცა მისცა?
განაღამცა გმორჩილობდით, თუ გვიბრძანო რაცა ვისცა!”
და იგი მონა აპატრონეს, ყველაკამან თაყვანი სცა.
stanzas.english_translation: Shermadin assembled together the courtiers and nobles; he showed them the letter in which he (Avt’handil) had told them his tidings. When they heard it, all remained heart-pierced, they beat themselves, there was not a tearless heart, not an unbruised breast.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 6 ('Letter of Avtandil to his Vassals', Stanza 176; Wardrop Stanza 174): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil writes an official charter to his nobles and troops instructing them to obey Shermadin as himself during his three-year absence, then rides out from his frontier city under the pretext of a border expedition before slipping away alone.

act_title: Act I: Arabia, The Royal Hunt & Quest for the Stranger Knight

location.desc: Realm of King Rostevan, Queen Tinatin, and Commander-in-Chief Avtandil.

key_maxim_ka: ხამს მოყვარე მოყვრისათვის თავი ჭირსა არ დამრიდად
key_maxim_en: A friend should not spare himself trouble for a friend's sake. (Stanza 162)
